title: Cryptocurrency in India — legal status, tax and risk
publisher: Artha Kavach summary of public guidance (RBI / SEBI / IRDAI / Income Tax Dept) — pending manual verification
text: Cryptocurrencies are not legal tender in India and are not regulated like shares or mutual funds, so there is no regulator you can complain to if an exchange fails or you are defrauded. Gains from selling crypto and other virtual digital assets are taxed at a flat 30% with no deduction for losses against other income, and a 1% TDS applies on each transfer above the threshold. Prices can fall 70–80% and many tokens go to zero; a large number of investment scams are built around 'crypto trading' apps and pig-butchering schemes. If you hold any, keep it a tiny fraction of your net worth that you can afford to lose, use only well-known exchanges registered with FIU-India, and never invest on the promise of guaranteed or daily returns.
summary_hinglish: India mein crypto legal tender nahi hai aur shares jaisa regulated bhi nahi, to fraud hone par shikayat karne ka regulator nahi. Crypto gains par flat 30% tax aur har transfer par 1% TDS lagta hai. Price 70-80% gir sakti hai. Guaranteed ya daily returns wale crypto apps scam hote hain.
summary_hi: भारत में क्रिप्टो वैध मुद्रा नहीं है और शेयरों जैसा विनियमित भी नहीं, इसलिए धोखाधड़ी पर शिकायत का कोई नियामक नहीं। क्रिप्टो लाभ पर 30% फ्लैट टैक्स और हर ट्रांसफर पर 1% TDS लगता है। कीमत 70-80% गिर सकती है। गारंटीड या रोज़ाना रिटर्न वाले क्रिप्टो ऐप धोखा होते हैं।
